 Heavy rains trigger flash floods in Kenya: Areas affected so far
 Saturday 31st October, 2026 02:28 PM | 
 By Aloys Michael 
 People stranded at Githurai roundabout after floods blocked the road. PHOTO/@Young_Pharmacie/X 
 Heavy rainfall pounding several parts of Kenya has t riggered flash floods, disrupted transport and forced emergency teams into search and rescue operation s, with Nairobi, the Rift Valley and coastal regions among the worst-affected areas.
 The persistent downpours have overwhelmed drainage systems, flooded major highways and left motorists stranded as rising water levels threaten homes, businesses and communities in vulnerable areas.
 The flooding comes as Kenya experiences the October-December short-rains season, with the Kenya Meteorological Department warning of continued enhanced rainfall across several counties.
 The Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS) and other emergency response teams are undertaking rescue operations in affected areas as concerns grow over the dangers posed by swollen rivers and flooded roads.
 Nairobi floods: Githurai, Parklands and major highways affected 
 Nairobi has experienced significant flooding following intense rainfall that has overwhelmed drainage infrastructure in several neighbourhoods.
 In Githurai, the main roundabout along Thika Road was among the worst-hit locations , with floodwater covering sections of the road, trapping vehicles and disrupting businesses.
 The situation was equally concerning in Parklands, where heavy water accumulation along First Avenue, near Oshwal School, submerged sections of the road and left motorists stranded.
 Major transport corridors, including Uhuru Highway and Waiyaki Way, also experienced heavy surface runoff, with public service vehicles and private motorists struggling to navigate flooded sections.
 The incidents highlight the growing vulnerability of Nairobi’s transport infrastructure during periods of intense rainfall.
 Floodwaters caused by heavy rains in Kajiado County. PHOTO/@KenyaRedCross/X. 
 Trans Mara floods: Lorry swept away at Mararianda Bridge 
 In the Rift Valley region, Trans Mara in Narok County has witnessed serious flooding after heavy upstream rainfall caused the Mara River to burst its banks.
 One of the most alarming incidents involved a lorry reportedly swept away while crossing the flooded Mararianda Bridge, triggering search and rescue efforts for passengers feared missing.
 Homes and livestock in several villages, including Emburgutio, have also been affected by rising water levels.
 In Kajiado South, rescue operations are reportedly underway in Baraka, Olkaria Village, following an incident in which a resident was swept away while attempting to cross an overflowing river.
 Tana River, Garissa, Lamu and Kilifi face flood threats 
 Flood concerns have also emerged across Kenya’s coastal and northeastern regions.
 In Tana River and Garissa counties, rising water levels along the Tana River have prompted warnings for communities living in low-lying settlements and areas prone to seasonal flooding .
 Further south along the coast, Lamu and Kilifi remain exposed to intense rainfall, thunderstorms and sudden flash floods.
 A flooded section of Parklands 1st Avenue at Oshwal school on Saturday, October 31, 2026. PHOTO/@parklandspamoja/X 
 The Kenya Meteorological Department has cautioned that enhanced rainfall could persist across several counties, increasing the possibility of flooding and damage to property.
 Authorities urge Kenyans to avoid flooded roads and rivers 
 As emergency response operations continue, residents have been urged to exercise extreme caution, particularly when travelling through flood-prone areas.
 The Kenya Red Cross Society’s ongoing rescue efforts underscore the importance of early reporting and community preparedness during flood emergencies.
 Motorists are advised to avoid driving through flooded roads and bridges, while pedestrians should stay away from swollen rivers and fast-flowing streams.
 Residents living near riverbanks have also been encouraged to monitor rising water levels and relocate to safer ground whenever necessary.
 The Kenya Meteorological Department’s rainfall warnings serve as an important reminder that the flood threat may persist even after heavy downpours subside, as water from upstream areas continues to flow into downstream communities.
 With more rainfall expected during the October-December short-rains season, Kenyans are being urged to remain alert, follow official weather updates and heed emergency advisories.
 The unfolding situation raises fresh questions about urban drainage, flood preparedness and the protection of communities living in flood-prone areas as Kenya navigates another challenging rainy season.
